prediction: The report provides an overview of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) conflict minerals disclosure rule and its implementation. It highlights that in 2017, 1,165 companies filed conflict minerals disclosures, similar to the previous two years. Most companies conducted country-of-origin inquiries, with 53% identifying the origin of conflict minerals. Due diligence was reported by 96% of companies, with 87% using the OECD framework. However, only 37% could confirm the minerals' source, and 47% could not determine if they funded armed groups. The report also discusses the rate of sexual violence in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and neighboring countries, noting that population-based surveys from 2016 and 2017 showed high prevalence rates. The findings underscore the ongoing challenges in tracing conflict minerals and the need for improved transparency and accountability in supply chains.
